text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, exactly one of three activities — A19, A20 and A25 — ran in virtually every trace: A19 in about 36 in 100 traces, A20 in about 31 and A25 in about 35, and the three practically never appeared together (their shares sum to about 100 in 100 with negligible overlap). In the later window all three have essentially disappeared from the sample: 0, 1 and 0 traces out of 200 respectively. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, REL007, REL009, REL014]
- In the earlier window, A41 fed this choice: about 33 in 100 of its outgoing transitions went to A19, about 33 to A25 and about 27 to A20, and A41 preceded each of the three in about 31–35 in 100 traces. In the later window, about 92 in 100 of A41's outgoing transitions go directly to A26, and A41 no longer co-occurs with any of the three. [DIR004, REL012, REL017, REL021]
- In the earlier window, each of the three activities led almost always onward to A26 (about 97–99 in 100 of their outgoing transitions; A19 preceded A26 in about 35 in 100 traces, A20 in about 30, A25 in about 34). In the later window these transitions are no longer observed. [DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, REL010, REL015, REL019]
- The gap between A41 and A26 closed accordingly: before, A26 followed A41 two steps later in about 94 in 100 cases (with one of the block activities in between); after, it follows one step later in about 93 in 100 cases. [LAG002]
- Small shifts consistent with this rerouting: A26's mean relative position moved slightly earlier (about 0.39 to 0.37 of the trace), A41's slightly later (about 0.32 to 0.33) and A14's slightly later (about 0.14 to 0.145); A14, A26 and A41 still occur in every trace in both windows. [POS001, POS005, POS006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the three-way choice between A19, A20 and A25 — seated between A41 and A26, with one of the three executed in nearly every trace before — is no longer executed in the later window, so that A41 now proceeds directly to A26. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, DIR004, LAG002]

- Participation in all three activities collapsed from about 31–36 in 100 traces to at most 1 in 200. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003]
- A41's routing flipped from a roughly even three-way split to about 92 in 100 transitions going straight to A26, and the A41-to-A26 distance shortened from two steps to one. [DIR004, LAG002]
- The relational items show the same disappearance consistently against A12, A14, A24, A26 and A41. [REL001, REL004, REL008, REL010, REL012, REL015, REL019, REL021]
- The screening produced 36 qualifying items where fewer than 1 would be expected for an unchanged process, so chance sampling cannot account for the evidence as a whole. [screening]

Limitations: the many relational items largely restate the same underlying trace behaviour and are not independent confirmations. [REL010, REL012, REL015, REL017, REL019, REL021] An important competing explanation remains: zero participation only means the activities were not observed, so with 200 traces per window a residual path in which the block still exists but is taken extremely rarely (A20 appeared once afterwards) cannot be distinguished from full removal. [OCC002]

Other differences: the spacing between A24 and A31 shifted from mostly two steps apart (about 59 in 100 cases) to mostly one step (about 60 in 100 cases) — plausibly a further knock-on of the rerouting, but the evidence does not tie it directly to the disappeared block. [LAG001]
